channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Embassy Warns of Mass Casualty Threat at Moscow Museum
item.description: The US embassy in Moscow said it was “aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event” on Saturday at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow, and was coordinating with Russian authorities on a response.
item.dc:creator: Ros Krasny

item.title: Israel’s Election Leaves Netanyahu in Limbo
item.description: Bloomberg Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner tells Bloomberg This Weekend that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition has a clear path to forming a government after Israel’s election, potentially setting up difficult coalition negotiations or another vote. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Bronner discusses Netanyahu’s political durability, increased Arab voter participation and how another conflict with Iran could alter the coalition calculus. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Kalshi, Polymarket Odds Don't Mimic Midterm Elections 2026 Polls
item.description: What may seem like contradictory numbers are, in fact, just two ways to capture a similar picture.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Silverman, Ella Feldman and Leonardo Nicoletti

item.title: Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil After Rejecting Election
item.description: Bloomberg Brazil Country Chief Filipe Pacheco tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after refusing to recognize Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory, as Bolsonaro faces multiple investigations in Brazil. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Pacheco explains Bolsonaro’s circuitous journey to Miami, his pledge to lead the opposition from the US and how investors are assessing Lula’s surprise comeback. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Midterm Fight Comes Down to the Final Days
item.description: Bloomberg Balance of Power co-host Joe Mathieu joins Bloomberg This Weekend to break down the final days of campaigning before the midterms, including President Donald Trump’s late push and the House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Meeks Puts Affordability Atop Democrats’ Agenda
item.description: House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks tells Bloomberg This Weekend that affordability would be Democrats’ top priority if they take control of the House, alongside restoring health-care benefits and conducting oversight of the Trump administration. Speaking with host David Gura, Meeks says companies involved in importing Russian diesel could face congressional scrutiny and predicts Hakeem Jeffries would become speaker if Democrats win the majority. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The AI Backlash Uniting Voters
item.description: Artificial intelligence is becoming a political issue for the first time in this year’s midterms, with much of the voter backlash focused not on the technology itself but on the data centers needed to power it. Communities from Michigan to Texas are raising concerns about electricity costs, water use and the broader impact of AI on jobs and local economies. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan says data centers have become a proxy for wider fears about AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Publicidad política en español cae antes de elecciones de EE.UU.
item.description: Las elecciones de medio término van camino a ser las más caras de la historia, pero los anuncios políticos en español se desploman pese al creciente peso del voto latino.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Midterm Elections 2026: Spending surge is leaving out Spanish-language ads
item.description: The US midterm elections are on track to be the most expensive ever, with ad spending set to top $11 billion, but the share being directed toward Spanish-language advertisements is shrinking dramatically, even with Latino voters seen by both parties as a critical swing group.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Investors Brace for Post-Midterm Policy Shifts
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Government Analyst Nathan Dean tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the midterm results could reshape congressional oversight while the Trump administration continues pursuing deregulation across banking, crypto and other industries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Dean explains what investors should watch in energy, AI, banking and trade, including the potential for further tariffs and changes that could encourage regional bank consolidation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Affordability Crisis Shaping US Elections
item.description: The US economy remains resilient, but many Americans are still struggling with the cost of housing, health care, groceries and other necessities. Former House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Kevin Brady and Willett Advisors Chairman & CEO Steven Rattner explain why the gap between strong economic data and household finances has made affordability one of the defining issues of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Starts at 'Basically Zero' in Building Cheap Military Drones
item.description: At a manufacturing plant near Salt Lake City with a big American flag on the wall and work stations crammed with tools and parts, dronemaker Vector Defense Inc. is in expansion mode.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Martin and Jen Judson

item.title: Cost of Living Looms Over the Midterms
item.description: Bloomberg Economics Economic Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that higher costs for gasoline, groceries and housing are weighing on voters and putting pressure on parts of the coalition Donald Trump assembled in 2024. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy explains how affordability concerns are playing out in states including Michigan, Iowa and Texas and how control of Congress could shape economic policy after the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Strikes Bashneft Refineries as Russia Attacks Power Grid
item.description: Ukraine’s drone forces struck a complex of refineries deep within Russia, even as Kyiv and other parts of the country struggled to restore electricity following overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Iran Threatens Wider US Strikes Even as Talks Make Progress
item.description: Iran’s Supreme Leader ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the US and Israel and expand Tehran’s options for retaliation, even as his top diplomat signaled progress in diplomatic talks.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Sykes

item.title: US Midterms: Trumpism May Already Be in Decline Worldwide
item.description: US elections from Alaska to Maine will reverberate globally next week, as midterm voting promises to diminish a president who has strong-armed the world.
item.dc:creator: Alan Crawford

item.title: Sánchez Rethinks Reelection Plan After Spain’s Rail Disaster
item.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez was planning a campaign based on optimism and charisma as Spain prepares to vote in four weeks.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Andy Burnham Had His Bounce. Now Things Are Set to Get Bumpy for New UK Premier
item.description: Britons gave Andy Burnham the benefit of the doubt in his first three months as prime minister. After an uninspiring budget, the next six weeks will test whether he can maintain the early momentum.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Chloe Chaplain and Lucy White

item.title: Polish President Holds Crisis Talks as Court Standoff Grows
item.description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki scheduled emergency consultations with parliamentary parties on Saturday to “restore constitutional order” as an escalating standoff at the country’s top court threatened to spark a political crisis.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Martewicz

item.title: Europe Braces for More Protests as Cost-of-Living Anger Grows
item.description: Cities in France, Germany and Italy were bracing for mass demonstrations on Saturday, with thousands of people expected to take to the streets to protest high living costs and other grievances with governments across Europe.
item.dc:creator: Ania Nussbaum, Michael Nienaber and Donato Paolo Mancini
